Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Nature & food

rural adjective

also country (as in country life), rustic, of the countryside, yokel, country bumpkin, peasant

classical

Cic. Rosc. Am. 75: vīta haec rūstica, quam tū agrestem vocās (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Fam. 16.21.7: rūsticus Rōmānus factus es
Traupman 410

rūsticus, rūstica, rūsticum

declension

of the country, rural

Of the country and of farming (rēs rūstica, agriculture); of people it is also plain, unsophisticated, and sometimes boorish, as against urbānus. For “in the country” say rūrī (see countryside).

Other words

  • agrestis, agreste — of the fields, rustic

    declension · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 2.16 (end): hospitiō agrestī (Lewis & Short)

    Of the land and the fields; of wild plants (see wild, of plants); and of people, more often than rūsticus, uncouth, coarse.

Examples

  • ōlim rūsticus urbānum mūrem mūs paupere fertur accēpisse cavō, veterem vetus hospes amīcum

    once upon a time, they say, a country mouse welcomed a town mouse in his poor hole, an old host his old friendHor. S. 2.6.79–81

  • nam rēs rūstica sīc est, sī ūnam rem sērō fēceris, omnia opera sērō faciēs

    for farming is like this: if you do one job late, you will do every job lateCato Agr. 5.7

  • rūsticus Rōmānus factus es

    you have become a Roman countrymanCic. Fam. 16.21.7

See also urban, countryside, farm, village, wild.
